title: Send money only to people you know

cards.text: The FTC says that once you send money through a payment app, it is hard to get back. The FCC says to never send money to someone you do not know.
cards.line: Fast money needs a careful check.

cards.text: Before you send, double-check the recipient name. The FTC says this helps make sure the payment goes to the right person.
cards.line: Check the name before you tap send.

cards.text: An unexpected request may be a scam. Talk with the person you know first, using a way you trust.
cards.line: A pause can protect your money.

checks.prompt: Why should you check before sending money?
options: It goes to the app maker
checks.why: The FTC says people may use payment apps to steal money because once you send it, it is hard to get back.

checks.prompt: What should you check before you send a payment?
checks.why: The FTC says to double-check the recipient information.

checks.prompt: A person you know appears to ask for money and wants it now. What is safest?
options: Ask a stranger to send it for you
checks.why: The FTC says to speak with the person to confirm an unexpected request.

takeaway: Check the name and pause before sending money.
